title: Longest increasing subsequence
summary: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of `nums`.
hints: Suppose a subsequence must end at position i. Which earlier elements could come directly before nums[i] in it?
For each position, the longest increasing subsequence ending there is 1 plus the best result among earlier positions holding a smaller value, or just 1 if there are none.
Make an array `longest` filled with 1. For each i, look at every j before it: if nums[j] < nums[i], longest[i] = max(longest[i], longest[j] + 1). The answer is the largest value in `longest`.
takeaway: Defining the sub-problem as "the best answer that ends exactly at i" is the step that unlocks many sequence problems. This version is O(n^2), which is fine for 2,500 elements; an O(n log n) version exists using binary search.
